name: sunlight_init_default
role: Sunlight init: sets ShadeStart/ShadeRange/Inclination (0x937aae/0x937aaf/0x937ab0) to the exe defaults 0x1c/0xf/0x20, and sunX/sunZ/sunBase (0x937aa8/0x937aaa/0x937aac) to the literal immediate **0x93 (147)**, all three - not derived from ShadeStart/ShadeRange/Inclination at all, a flat hardcoded constant - then calls sunlight_init_2 (0x401790). Live-measured this session on two running levels with different on-disk Inclination (0x40/0x20): sunX=sunZ=sunBase=147 in both, turn 20 and turn 77 (9+ multiples of the 8-turn tick 0x401350 checks), confirming the level's own sunlight block never visibly moves the vector away from this flat default in normal play - see 0x401350/0x401920/0x4be230 - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

Near-duplicate of part of sunlight_init_default: sets sunX/sunZ/sunBase to the same flat 0x93 (147) without touching ShadeStart/ShadeRange/Inclination, then falls through into sunlight_init_2 (0x401790) - a "reset the light vector to flat" helper reused from more than one call site

Per-turn sun-angle tick, gated: no-op unless flag bit 0x895da5&0x8 is set (live-measured this session: it isn't, in normal single-level play - Inclination stayed at its on-disk value across 9+ ticks, see 0x401040); when set and the turn counter's low 3 bits are all 1 (every 8th turn), increments Inclination (0x937ab0) by 1 and recomputes sunX/sunBase (0x937aa8/0x937aac) from REAL sin/cos tables indexed by the new Inclination (0x5de5e8/0x5ddde8, scaled), then calls sunlight_init_2 (0x401790) - this, not the level's static sunlight block, is the exe's actual day/night-style sun-angle animation mechanism, and it appears disabled in the sessions measured this session

Builds two unrelated 1024-entry angle-keyed shade tables (0x89bc8e, 0x89c08d) from the sin/cos tables (0x5ddde8/0x5de5e8) dotted against the sun vector (0x937aa8/0x937aaa/0x937aac) and ShadeStart/ShadeRange (0x937aae/0x937aaf); does not itself write the sun vector, only reads it - role of the two output tables not traced further this session

Unconditionally forces Inclination (0x937ab0) to 0x40 (64, overwriting whatever the level set) and sunX/sunBase (0x937aa8/0x937aac) from two FIXED scalar memory cells, 0x5de9e8/0x5de1e8 - NOT an array indexed by Inclination (no writes to either address found anywhere in the exe's code this session, so they are build-time data constants, not computed from the level's sunlight block) - then calls sunlight_init_2 (0x401790); gated behind flag bit 0x895da5&0x8 like 0x401350, same early-return. Despite the name "Inclination=64 init path" this is not a per-Inclination branch - it hardcodes a SINGLE fixed result whenever it runs

role: Runs a class-1 person's active command-group order each turn (called as fn(unit) from unit_processing_class_1_person at 0x4d351a, for state 0xA "carrying out an order"): resolves the unit's active command-group id (word at unit+0x9b if nonzero, else unit+0x8b[(byte)unit+0xa6] - corrects an earlier draft of this row, which called 0x938830 a "per-unit lookup table": it is a per-GROUP array shared by every unit currently assigned to that group via 0x436d00/0x436c20, see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Command groups") and, when a real group is assigned, reads that group record's kind byte (group+0x0), subtracts 3, and jumps through a 31-entry table at 0x432d18 covering kinds 3-33 (the odd/even "going to place"/"doing it" pairs) to the per-kind handler, e.g. kind 19 and 21 both call the attack-order handler 0x51A2A0, kind 33 calls the preach-order handler 0x43C7A0; two unread special branches at 0x432a5d/0x432a65 gate on the group record's +0x1 bit 0x1 or the unit's own +0x13 bit 0x10; when neither +0x9b nor any +0x8b[+0xa6] secondary slot resolves to a live group, does only minor housekeeping (facing/cell via 0x405050/0x402e70, no position write) and returns 0 - confirmed, a person with nothing assigned does nothing and never wanders; the shared tail at 0x432a3e also calls add_unit_to_formation (0x5018c0) whenever global flag 0x895da6 bit 0x4 and the unit's own +0x76 bit 0x8 (copied by 0x432df0 from the current group's kind-flags byte+0xa bit 0x10) are both set - see 0x5018c0/0x501000 "Command groups" formations

is_within(pos_a*, half_width, pos_b*, 2): returns 1 iff |pos_a.x - pos_b.x| < half_width and |pos_a.z - pos_b.z| < half_width (both axes), else 0; used by state 6 (0x4d342a) as the "have I arrived at my destination" check with half_width=0x38 (56 world units).

name: order_set
role: Writes a command group's shared order ("add an order to a group" in pop3-rev-analysis.md's Reference table; corrects an earlier draft of this row, which called the 1st arg a "unit_id" - it is a group id, see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Command groups"), called as fn(group_id, kind, target_or_pos_ptr, extra_flags): writes into that group's 10-byte slot in the 0x938830 array (slot = group_id*10 + 0x938830) - if the slot already holds this exact kind AND the same target/position dword at slot+0x6, it is a complete no-op (returns immediately, verified: no position-rounding or state change happens on this path); otherwise sets slot+0x0 = kind, ORs extra_flags into slot+0x1, copies *target_or_pos_ptr into slot+0x6, then derives a snapped/line-of-sight-adjusted position (per-kind flags DWORD from a table at 0x5a7dc0+kind*22+0xa, confirmed stride 22 bytes/kind this session, select rounding via 0x4044b0 and a per-direction table at 0x8a03e4) back into slot+0x6/+0x8; at the very end, if that same per-kind flags DWORD has bit 0x80000 set and the slot's own target id resolves (table 0x890390) to a live unit whose own +0x9d field has bit 0x80 set, it OVERWRITES the slot's kind to 0xA (10) while keeping the same target id; of its ~37 call sites, most pass extra_flags=0 (via an explicitly-zeroed register) or the literal 0x20 (0x20 is confirmed this session: 0x51FF60 skips the auto-attack-radius lookup for any group with flags bit 0x20 set); only one call site found this session (0x41cd6f, in an unrelated per-tribe function 0x41cc20 using order kind 0x1c/28) passes the literal 0x40 that 0x51C3C0 checks for preacher targeting - the call site that sets 0x40 for an actual preach order (if any) was not found and is the next concrete lead for "Preacher conversion"

name: preach_order_handler
role: Preach order (kind 33) per-turn handler, called as fn(preacher) from order_execute's (0x432590) kind-dispatch table - takes a 2nd "order slot" arg by the same convention as other kind handlers but never reads it; instead resolves its own target live each call from the preacher's own +0x89 field (seeded from +0x72 on first entry) via unit table 0x890390, into a local "target" pointer (called edi below, NOT the order slot): while preacher substate (preacher+0x2d) is 1 "approaching", checks the target's building occupancy against a population-cap-like pair of fields (building+0x96 vs +0x9a via building lookup 0x508f70) and, failing that, on closing to ~12 units sets substate 2 (or 4 if target+0x76 == 0x99); substates 1-3 walk toward the target, substates 4-8 stop and face it (0x4458d0); substates (1-9 remapped via 0x43d010) and (2-9) branch through two more inline jump tables at 0x43d004/0x43d01c; the terminal substate-8 body (0x43cd77) is the actual payoff: plays sound 0x9f on the TARGET, sets the target's own state (target+0x2c) to 5, and rewrites the target's internal animation-sequence kinds to 0x98/0x9b/0x99 over 40 ticks via 0x4f14b0 (same helper also used on the preacher's own substates elsewhere in this function, likely a generic "overlay effect sequence" setter, not an order) - this is the confirmed link from the preach order to the target, but it sets state 5, not the "struck" state 3 from pop3-rev-analysis.md "Preacher conversion"; see 0x4d6970 for why state 5 is probably unrelated to conversion, and 0x51c3c0 for the actual (still unfound) state-3 trigger candidate

name: compute_cell_light
role: Per-cell landscape-texture brightness byte (map-cell +0xd, table 0x8a03e4): `clamp((sunBase + dz*sunZ - dx*sunX)/350 + (low_nibble(+0xe)+8)*16, 0, 255)` where dx/dz are height deltas to the cell's own +2 neighbours and sunX/sunZ/sunBase are the level's sun vector (0x937aa8/0x937aaa/0x937aac); called from level_land_processing_2 (0x44df40) per dirty cell after every height edit, so it tracks terrain edits live, not baked once at load - resolves the map-cell +0xe low nibble's previously-unidentified role. Live-measured this session on two running levels (on-disk Inclination 0x40 and 0x20, both ShadeStart=28/ShadeRange=15): sunX=sunZ=sunBase=**147 in both**, confirming (with 0x401040) this is the flat hardcoded constant, not derived per-level - open-populous's `SunParams::from_sunlight` guess (180/225/280, varying by ShadeRange/ShadeStart) has no basis; the right fix is a flat 147/147/147 unless 0x401350's gated day/night tick turns out to be active in some game mode. Flat cells (dx=dz=0) read light=128 exactly live, matching `clamp(147/350 + 128, 0, 255)` with the 147/350 term flooring to 0. A live spot-check on sloped cells did NOT reproduce the formula from a naive `base+(z*128+x)*16` cell-address read (see dis.txt around 0x4be259/0x4be261: the packed-index build masks x/z with `0xFE`/`0xFE00` before scaling, which a plain row-major address calc does not reproduce bit-for-bit) - attributed to that addressing gap in the one-off measurement script, not the formula, which the disassembly confirms matches the existing doc exactly. First pass 2026-10-20 claimed the masking was inert and a plain height(x,z)/height(x+2,z) (real 0..127 coords) reproduced it bit-for-bit - WRONG, caught and corrected same session. Corrected, cross-checked against load_level2's height-table populate loop (0x484c9a-0x484cb8: exactly 0x4000=16384=128*128 iterations, table pointer += 0x10 flat EVERY iteration, reads the file's height values sequentially in its own (z*128+x) order) - that proves table 0x8a03e4's real layout is `base+16*(z_real*128+x_real)`, one record per real file cell, no doubling. For compute_cell_light's own formula `base+(x&0xfe)*8+(z&0xfe)*1024` to hit that same record, its raw x/z must equal 2*x_real/2*z_real - its coordinate unit is DOUBLE the real file-cell grid. So its "+2" neighbour step lands on real cell x_real+1 (one real cell over), not x_real+2. open-populous's height(x,z) takes real 0..127 file-cell coords directly (confirmed byte-for-byte against levl2001.dat), so `height(x,z)-height(x+2,z)` measures across two real cells where the original measures across one - overshoot confirmed, not refuted. Fix belongs in open-populous game_core::shading::cell_light: neighbour should be height(x+1,z)/height(x,z+1), not +2 - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

name: set_texture_landscape_main
role: Per-quad landscape colouring: for the 4 cells forming a drawn quad ((x,z),(x+2,z),(x+2,z+2),(x,z+2)), each corner samples THAT cell's own blend (+0xa, table 0x8a03e4) directly (no cross-cell averaging at this step) to pick a cliff-palette row (blend/4, table 0x5d45cc) and to bump its own altitude-colour index (height+0x4b, +0x4b again if blend!=0, clamp 0x3fe); both values are then interpolated smoothly across the quad like ordinary vertex colours (per-corner deltas scaled <<0xc for the fill) - this ordinary per-corner interpolation, not anything lava-specific, is why adjoining hot cells read as a soft round blob per cell that visually fuses where two hot cells share an edge; no turn counter, PRNG or oscillator read anywhere in this function - "Building ashes" "Drawn". The same altitude-colour index also doubles as the bigfade row: it is looked up into DISP_SENSITIVITY (0x5d45b8) to scale a signed disp noise sample into a row jitter, combined with the quad's interpolated map-cell +0xd brightness byte (also corner-sampled/interpolated, see compute_cell_light 0x4be230) into one flat index into bigf0-X.dat, whose output (0..111) is the `colour` fed into the cliff lookup above - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour". Re-read 2026-10-20: after computing the quad's 4 corner values it dispatches to one of landscape_texture_32/16/16_fade (0x4bf860/0x4c0380/0x4c0ec0) to actually fill the pixels - no D3D/vtable call anywhere in any of the three, confirming the landscape is CPU-rasterized per rendered pixel at the quad's own on-screen extent, not drawn as a GPU-textured, pre-baked bitmap (see those rows). Re-read 2026-10-20 again: its own preamble, before any of that corner/quad math, walks a list of mesh vertex-grid points and reads each one's own cell +0xc low nibble (the coastal shape, table 0x5aa328, same field "Parking and the shore" documents for vehicle parking) - testing bit 0x2 of the shape's class byte ("open sea") to skip the land-colour computation entirely for a pure-open-sea point, confirming land AND shore cells (shapes 0, 2-15) both go through the full blend/bigfade/cliff pipeline above (so a coastline's own steep land/seabed height delta legitimately pushes blend high there, giving the shore its rockier "cliff" colouring) while pure sea alone is excluded and drawn separately

name: drowning_check
role: Per-turn "is this unit drowning here" predicate (2 callers: 0x4D43A0 life-step, 0x502910 spirit-setup). Escapes (all -> not drowning): flags +0xC bit 0x2; a per-instance exemption table 0x5A7BA8[+0x30] bit 0x2 (checked indices 0-11, none set it - no person type is exempt via this table); airborne (+0xC bit 0x80000); standing above the real ground/water height (calc_point_height 0x44E940 vs +0x41, e.g. a boat deck); is_land_at (0x44F980) true (solid support, also clears +0x10 bit 0x1000000); inside something (+0x9F != 0). Otherwise re-derives the FINE per-pixel coastal shape (same 0x5AA328 mechanism as 0x4D4A00, testing only byte+0 bits 0x3C, no byte+4 gate) at the unit's exact current position: shape 0 (pure land) or 1 (pure sea) -> drown; any boundary shape 2-15 -> drown unless flags +0x10 bit 0x1000000 is set. Defaults to "drowning" - only specific supports prevent it; a "shore-shaped" cell (per-cell granularity) is not inherently safe at the fine-grained level.

Class-10 state-12 ("spirit rise") sub-state dispatcher, keyed by +0x2D (0-6, table 0x502E8C): 0 -> 0x5029EF (calm, stationary), 1 -> 0x502A5C, 2 -> 0x502AEA, 3 -> 0x502BA3 (climbing + spin), 4 -> 0x502CDB, 5 -> 0x502D7E, 6 -> 0x502E7A (sub-states 1,2,4,5,6 not read this session).

Spirit sub-state 0 ("calm ghost" rise, entered by any non-wildman type NOT dying in a drowning-eligible spot): 4-turn timer; per-type object id from table 0x5A6EA6 -> VSTART 38 (followers, tint by draw-class 14-18) or 85 (shaman). No altitude change - a stationary animation, not a climb. Timer 0 -> sub-state 1.

Spirit sub-state 3 ("climbing" rise, ALWAYS entered for a wildman regardless of cause of death; entered for any other type only if it died in a drowning-eligible spot): 32-turn timer; per-type object id from table 0x5A6EB8 -> VSTART 31 for wild (the SAME clip already documented as the "flung in the air" blast-knockback tumble animation), 40 for followers, 45 for shaman. Every turn: altitude (+0x41) += 0x28 (40 world units, ~2.5 cells over the full 32 turns, no gravity/deceleration - a real sustained vertical launch); when the copied type (+0x74) == 1 (wildman) ONLY, additionally spins facing (+0x26) += 0x5B (91/2048) every turn - a continuous spin found nowhere else in the engine; optional shaman-only scenery-burst spawn gated on +0x77. Timer 0 -> sub-state 4. This is the mechanism behind "a wildman's death looks like flying into the sky, not a calm rising ghost" - it is the SAME code path anyone dying in water gets, but wildmen get it unconditionally plus the extra spin.
